page: Microsoft Azure M832s_12_v3 is an ultra-high-memory instance belonging to the MSHighMemoryv3 family. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization and powered by an x86_64 Intel processor architecture, the instance provides 832 dedicated virtual CPUs and 11,400.0 GB of system memory. This yields a dense memory-to-core ratio of 13.7 GB per vCPU, specifically targeting workloads that exceed conventional multi-terabyte system memory footprints.

Hardware capabilities do not include local disk storage or hardware GPU acceleration. Storage must be provisioned via remote Premium Storage volumes, making disk architecture design dependent on network-attached persistence. While dedicated compute resources minimize hypervisor contention across all 832 vCPUs, the lack of local temporary or ephemeral scratch space requires external volume attachment for operating system and application data.

From a qualitative cost and infrastructure perspective, the M832s_12_v3 consolidates massive workloads onto a single host node. This resource density reduces the operational and network latency complexities of distributed multi-node clustering. It provides an efficient scale-up path for massive enterprise database platforms, including SAP HANA, large-scale in-memory relational databases, and enterprise resource planning systems that demand massive coherent memory address spaces.
description: Microsoft Azure M832s_12_v3 is a memory-optimized instance from the MSHighMemoryv3 family engineered for extreme memory-bound enterprise applications. Powered by Intel x86_64 processors, the instance delivers 832 dedicated vCPUs alongside 11,400.0 GB of memory, equating to 13.7 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance incorporates zero local disk storage and features no dedicated GPU hardware accelerators, necessitating the integration of Azure Premium Storage for persistent file systems and operating systems. By scaling up to eleven terabytes of memory within a single virtualized host on Microsoft Hyper-V, the M832s_12_v3 avoids the architectural overhead associated with distributed computing environments. It functions primarily as a scale-up foundation for mission-critical in-memory databases, including massive SAP HANA environments, real-time analytics engines, and enterprise data warehousing workloads requiring unified memory access across hundreds of dedicated compute threads.
